slint-interpreter 1.18.1 from crates.io with two changes, both in ItemTree::item_geometry (search for "Telescope patch"): ItemTree::item_geometry no longer clones
the item's geometry expression and no longer builds a Struct from it.

Why: Slint asks every item for its geometry on every walk of the item tree (rendering, hit testing, dirty tracking). The interpreter answered by cloning the
whole geometry expression (a deep copy of an expression tree, allocating) and evaluating it into a Value::Struct (a HashMap of SmolStr to Value, allocating
again), then read x, y, width and height back out of the map. A profile of the desktop window at 4K with every plugin loaded showed that walk at about 46 %
of the window thread, malloc, free and memmove at about 40 % of it.

What it does now: the expression is borrowed from the compilation unit (the cell is only borrowed while it is read, as before), and when it is the usual
Expression::Struct the four fields are evaluated one by one, in the order upstream gets them from the field map (height, width, x, y), because evaluating height can create a ComponentContainer's component, which x reads. Any other expression shape takes the old path, so results are the same. The dependencies the
evaluation reads are tracked exactly as before, because the same sub-expressions are evaluated in the same context.

Second change, in item_tree_vtable.rs and instance.rs (search for "Telescope patch"): ItemTree::item_geometry now remembers each item's rect. Instance has one cache entry per flat tree index
(created on first use) holding the last rect and a PropertyTracker. The geometry is only evaluated again when the tracker is dirty, that is when a property the geometry expression read has changed;
the tracker is registered as a dependency of whatever is being evaluated (the window's redraw tracker, a layout), so a change reaches them as it did before. One difference: evaluating an item's geometry can itself change a property it already read (a ComponentContainer creating its component), and a tracker forgets a change made while it evaluates. So a dirty entry is evaluated until two passes in a row agree (at most 4), which costs extra only when the entry was dirty. The renderer (femtovg has no
partial rendering) still walks every item that is not inside a cached layer on each frame, so this makes each visit cheap instead of making fewer visits. Items in a repeated row live in their own
Instance, so a repeater adding or removing rows never reuses an entry for a different item.

Measured (release, window thread CPU over 40 s after 25 s warm-up, fake phone, headless nested KWin, one run each):
  4K, everything loaded and on:  15.77 % -> 13.32 % (15 % less)
  4K, nothing loaded:             3.75 % ->  3.15 % (16 % less)
  1080p, everything loaded and on: 12.77 % -> 10.25 % (20 % less)
  1080p, nothing loaded:          2.80 % ->  2.37 % (15 % less)
The main window and the Settings window drew byte for byte the same before and after.

Measured with the cache on top (same setup, two runs each, base then patched back to back): 4K all on 13.5 -> 11.5 %, 4K nothing loaded 3.1 -> 3.1 % (no change, within noise), 1080p all on 10.3 -> 8.6 %, 1080p nothing loaded 2.2 -> 1.85 %.
Pixels: the main window, Settings, a resize, and a card folding and unfolding (mid-animation too) drew byte for byte the same.

Drop it when Slint stops cloning and boxing in item_geometry (nothing upstream is known yet; check the release notes after 1.18.1), then remove this folder and the
slint-interpreter line under [patch.crates-io] in rust/Cargo.toml. Tests and the lockfile were left out of the copy, and so were the [[test]] entries for them in Cargo.toml.
Slint's GPL-3 option is what Telescope uses; the licence files are kept in LICENSES.
